# SPAS

> SPAS (Secure Private Asset Sync) is an open-source command-line tool for developers. It keeps files that should not be in a project's main Git repository, such as test data, local setup, AI instructions, roadmaps, and internal docs, at their normal paths in the workspace. SPAS excludes them from the main repository through `.git/info/exclude`, versions them in a separate GitHub repository, and writes them back to the same paths on other machines and for teammates who link that repository.

Key facts:

- Platforms: Linux, macOS, and Windows on amd64 and arm64.
- Requirements: Git 2.43.1 or newer, and Git credentials (SSH or HTTPS) with access to the linked GitHub repository.
- License: AGPL-3.0. Free to use.
- Commands: `link`, `add`, `remove`, `sync`, `status`, `diff`, `doctor`, `unlink`, `completion`, `version`.
- SPAS never edits the project's `.gitignore`. It writes a fenced block in `.git/info/exclude`.
- Managed files are stored as ordinary Git content in the linked GitHub repository. SPAS does not encrypt them; keep that repository private. Except in dry runs, `spas link` and `spas sync` run an anonymous `git ls-remote` probe and print a warning if the repository is publicly readable. The warning does not block the command, and a failed probe does not prove the repository is private.
- Only repositories on github.com are supported.
- SPAS manages regular files (Git modes 100644 and 100755) that the main repository does not track. Adding a folder enrolls the regular files currently inside it. Symlinks, directory junctions, submodules, Git LFS pointers, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, and `.gitmodules` are rejected.
- Filenames follow each machine's Git and filesystem rules. A name such as `notes:2026.md` works on Linux but not on Windows; SPAS reports the failing path instead of renaming the file.
- `spas unlink` keeps workspace files by default. `--remove-files` deletes synced files, and discarding unsynced changes needs separate approval (`--discard-unsynced-changes` in scripts).
- Scriptable: `--json` output, `--non-interactive` mode, explicit policy flags, `--timeout` deadlines, and documented exit codes. Unattended runs turn off Git and SSH credential prompts, so credentials must be set up before the run.

## Install

- Homebrew (macOS, Linux; formula that builds from source): `brew install getspas/tap/spas`
- Scoop (Windows): `scoop bucket add getspas https://github.com/getspas/scoop-bucket`, then `scoop install getspas/spas`
- Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, and compatible systems: download the .deb or .rpm from https://github.com/getspas/spas/releases/latest and follow the installation guide.
- From source (Go 1.26.9 or newer): `go install -trimpath github.com/getspas/spas@latest`

## Quick start

```bash
# in the project workspace, with an empty GitHub repository for the files
spas link your-org/project-assets --transport ssh --branch main
spas add testdata/ .env.local AGENTS.md
spas sync --dry-run
spas sync
```

On another machine or for a teammate: clone the project, run `spas link your-org/project-assets --transport ssh`, then `spas sync`.

- [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/getspas/spas/wiki/Troubleshooting): diagnose errors with `spas doctor`
